data.gender_notes: Faden is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old German word ‘fad’, meaning a thread or cord. In Christian symbolism, a cord can represent the connection between God and humanity, or the bond of marriage. The name Faden carries the meaning “Thread, Cord” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Faden usually hope their child will grow to embody thread, cord and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Faden belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Thread, Cord.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Faden total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: In the name Faden, the Old German origin suggests strength, durability, and connection. This Germanic influence can be traced back to the early European settlers in North America, where the name has continued to be passed down through generations.
data.spiritual_significance: In a Christian context, the name Faden has a profound spiritual meaning. It is derived from the Old German word 'fad,' meaning a thread or cord. This biblical reference can evoke the image of the connection between God and humanity. In faith, we trust in the divine cord that binds our souls to the Almighty. Additionally, in the context of marriage, the name Faden symbolizes the unbreakable bond between husband and wife, representing the divine union intended for representatives of God on earth.
